subject: Decision Making
title: Auto-Enrollment in Savings
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Auto-Enrollment in Savings.

hook.text: Most Americans said they wanted to save for retirement. Almost none actually enrolled in 401k plans.

buildup.text: Companies switched from opt-in to auto-enrollment. New employees were enrolled by default. They could opt out anytime.

discovery.text: Enrollment jumped from 49% to 86%. People always wanted to save. They just never got around to filling out the form.

twist.text: Thaler's Save More Tomorrow program auto-increased contributions with each raise. People saved more without noticing.

climax.text: Auto-enrollment proved defaults can close the gap between intention and action without forcing anyone to do anything.

punchline.text: 49% to 86% enrollment. Same plan. One checkbox changed everything.

quiz.question: What happened when 401k plans switched to auto-enrollment?
options: Enrollment jumped from 49% to 86% because the default was changed to enrolled
